passages.provision_quote: Resentencing pursuant to this section shall result in a lesser sentence than the one originally imposed as a result of the elimination of the repealed enhancement, unless the court finds by clear and convincing evidence that imposing a lesser sentence would endanger public safety.
passages.note: Authored bill retroactively invalidates certain sentencing enhancements and defaults to a lesser sentence absent a public-safety finding, showing a leniency direction without matching any single rung's full clauses.

rows.reasoning: As the bill's author, Allen's SB 483 (2021-2022) retroactively invalidates specified sentencing enhancements and requires courts to impose a sentence that 'shall result in a lesser sentence than the one originally imposed... unless the court finds by clear and convincing evidence that imposing a lesser sentence would endanger public safety,' showing only a lean toward reduced punishment. This narrow enhancement-removal measure does not establish 'support and treatment, not punishment,' 'service or restitution,' or a stated 'each situation is different' orientation, so the evidence is direction-only.
